wisdom.content: Cached prompt tokens are NOT free, and the discount ratio varies ~2x by vendor. Moonshot Kimi K2.7 Code: cache-hit $0.19/M vs fresh $0.95/M = 0.20x. Anthropic is 0.10x; OpenAI 0.25-0.50x. Measured adv-engineer spend 2026-07-21..27: 25,890 calls, 2,707M cached-read tokens, and 78% of the $660 total was cached-input re-read (not misses — cache hit rate was 0.95 with zero mid-session model switches). Implication for ADV: fixed prompt weight (tool schemas, instructions, agent prompt) is paid on EVERY turn at 20% rate. "It's cached so it's free" is false. Reducing injected tool-schema weight has direct measurable cost impact. Source: platform.kimi.ai/docs/pricing/chat-k27-code, dev.opencode.ai/docs/go, Fireworks launch post.

OpenCode v1.18.7 verified facts about agent prompt assembly (pinned source, packages/): (1) Config `instructions[]` AND global/project AGENTS.md inject into EVERY session including spawned sub-agents — `Instruction.system()` (session/instruction.ts:152-177) takes no agent argument. (2) There is NO per-agent instruction exclusion mechanism; the agent schema (core/src/v1/config/agent.ts:10-41) has no `instructions` field. So every token in the global instructions array is multiplied across every agent lane. (3) `tools:` frontmatter is DEPRECATED and normalizes to the same permission ruleset as `permission:`, with explicit `permission:` merging OVER it (agent.ts:67-81) — a per-agent `permission` block in opencode.jsonc overrides the generated manifest. (4) Code Mode (`OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_CODE_MODE=true`) removes MCP tools from top-level and exposes `execute` instead (session/tools.ts:383-390); plugin tools are NOT affected. The `execute` catalog is budgeted at 2,000 estimated tokens with `PARTIAL - N of M shown` truncation (codemode/src/tool-runtime.ts:86-88). Re-verify against the deployed binary before relying on any of this — upstream `dev` and pinned 1.18.7 gave contradictory answers on whether denied tools are filtered from the payload.

documents.proposal:
# Fix malformed agent-manifest frontmatter and guard against recurrence

## Why

ADV agent manifests declare per-agent tool surfaces. In seven of twelve, that declaration has no effect: the frontmatter does not parse, so OpenCode drops the `tools:` map entirely and the agent receives every registered tool.

This was proven empirically, not inferred. It is a live defect affecting the orchestrator's own authority boundary.

## Root Cause Analysis

**Defect origin:** Agent manifests silently fail to restrict tools. Declared denials — both ADV plugin tools and non-ADV tools — have no runtime effect in affected manifests.

**Evidence gathered:**

*Tier 1 (local, empirical):*

Three live sub-agent probes measured the actual tool surface each lane receives:

| Lane | note in frontmatter | frontmatter YAML | `opencode.jsonc` `permission:` | predicted adv tools | observed |
|---|---|---|---|--:|--:|
| `adv-verifier` | no | parses | none | 11 (Tier 1) | **11** |
| `adv-tron` | yes | fails | none | all | **88** |
| `adv-researcher` | yes | fails | yes, 9 allows | 9 | **9** |
| `adv` (orchestrator) | yes | fails | none for `adv_*` | all | **88** |

Prediction accuracy 4/4. `adv-verifier` additionally confirmed built-in denials apply when frontmatter parses: `write`, `edit`, `task`, `question`, `todowrite` absent; `bash`, `read` present; Code Mode `tools.adv` filtered to 2 entries.

Frontmatter validated with a JS YAML parser (the parser family OpenCode uses), not only Python, to exclude a strictness false positive. Result — repo `.opencode/agents/`: 5 parse, 7 fail. Deployed `~/.config/opencode/agents/`: 8 parse, 5 fail. Every failure correlates 1:1 with the note appearing inside frontmatter; no failure occurs without it.

Parser error, verbatim: `Implicit keys need to be on a single line`.

*Tier 2 (external):* Not required. The mechanism is fully observable locally and was confirmed behaviorally in live sessions.

**Leading hypothesis (confirmed):** `> **Invoke routing:** …` was inserted inside the YAML frontmatter block. YAML treats a leading `>` as a folded-block-scalar indicator; with no key it is a syntax error. OpenCode discards the unparseable frontmatter's `tools:` map and applies no restriction. Introduced by commit `faabcac6b` (2026-07-25).

**Ruled-out paths:**

- *OpenCode does not filter plugin-tool schemas.* Refuted — `adv-verifier` receives exactly its declared 11.
- *`tools:` frontmatter is visibility-inert while `permission:` is not.* Refuted by the same result.
- *Tool-name wildcard mismatch (`mcp_Adv_*` vs `adv_*`).* Refuted — all probes report plain `adv_spec`. The prefixed form was an artifact of one harness's presentation layer, not OpenCode.
- *ADV's tiering architecture is wrong.* Refuted — the architecture is sound and works wherever frontmatter parses.

**Why CI did not catch it:**

| Guard | Behavior | Gap |
|---|---|---|
| `pnpm run generate:manifests:check` | diffs ADV-GENERATED block content | never parses frontmatter as YAML |
| `plugin/src/tier4-manifest-awareness.test.ts:17` | asserts the note is present | asserts presence, never placement |
| `plugin/scripts/generate-agent-manifests.ts:270-274` | rewrites the note via regex | preserves and perpetuates the bad placement |

A test required the note to exist; nothing verified the file still parsed. Prose assertion without structural validation (P33).

**Spec-law impact:** No existing requirement governs agent-manifest frontmatter validity. A new requirement under the agent-manifest capability is warranted so manifest parseability becomes spec law rather than convention.

**Bypass rationale:** RCA was produced inline rather than via `/adv-problem` because the investigation was already complete — the defect was discovered during proof-of-concept measurement for this change's original investigative scope, with the mechanism traced end to end before the proposal gate.

## What Changes

1. Move the `> **Invoke routing:**` note out of frontmatter into the prompt body (after the closing `---`) in all affected manifests.
2. Update `generate-agent-manifests.ts` so it writes and maintains the note in the body, never inside frontmatter.
3. Strengthen the placement assertion: `tier4-manifest-awareness.test.ts` must assert the note is present **and** outside frontmatter.
4. Add structural validation to `pnpm run check`: every shipped agent manifest must have parseable YAML frontmatter, and every manifest declaring ADV tool policy must yield a non-empty `tools:` map.
5. Redeploy so `~/.config/opencode/agents/` carries corrected manifests.

## User Outcomes

- Each ADV agent operates with the tool surface its manifest declares — no more, no less.
- The orchestrator's intended authority boundary is actually enforced, restoring defense-in-depth ahead of ADV's own role firewall.
- A manifest that would silently lose its restrictions fails the build instead of shipping.
- Removing the `opencode.jsonc` permission drift in the parallel toolbox change becomes safe rather than exposing four lanes.
- Agents stop carrying tool schemas they cannot use.

## Scope

### In Scope

- `.opencode/agents/*.md` — the 7 manifests with unparseable frontmatter: `adv`, `adv-designer`, `adv-engineer`, `adv-researcher`, `adv-tron`, `adv-visual-review`, `plan`.
- `plugin/scripts/generate-agent-manifests.ts` — note placement logic.
- `plugin/src/tier4-manifest-awareness.test.ts` — placement assertion.
- New frontmatter-validity check wired into `pnpm run check`.
- Post-fix empirical re-verification of at least the `adv` and `adv-tron` lanes.
- Redeploy of corrected manifests via `scripts/deploy-local.sh`.

### Out of Scope

- Changing which tools any agent is granted. Placement is corrected; grant lists are untouched.
- Re-tiering the ADV tool surface (`auditTierAdvToolExposure`).
- Tool-family consolidation (`raiseToolSurfaceBarConsolidate`).
- Sub-agent prompt-body routing for `adv_subagent_report_submit` / `adv_run_test` (`fixSubagentReportRouting`).
- `opencode.jsonc` permission-drift removal — toolbox-owned, tracked in the parallel session.
- Any change to OpenCode itself.

### Must Not

- Must not alter any agent's `allowed` tool set while relocating the note — a fix that changes grants is a different change.
- Must not silence, delete, or weaken the invoke-routing note to make parsing succeed; the note is load-bearing guidance and must survive in the body.
- Must not deploy from a worktree — deploy runs from merged trunk only.
- Must not treat "YAML now parses" as sufficient evidence; empirical re-probe of the observed tool count is required before acceptance.
- Must not hand-edit deployed manifests in `~/.config/opencode/agents/` — they are generated and deployed artifacts.

## Affected Code

`.opencode/agents/*.md` (7 files) · `plugin/scripts/generate-agent-manifests.ts` · `plugin/src/tier4-manifest-awareness.test.ts` · `plugin/package.json` check pipeline · new validation module under `plugin/scripts/` or `plugin/src/`.

## Constraints

- `pnpm run generate:manifests:check` must stay green.
- Deploy runs from merged trunk, never a worktree.
- The new check must cover both repo and deployed manifest locations, or clearly state which it governs.

## Impact

Restores intended authority boundaries on the orchestrator and `adv-tron`; removes unusable tool schemas from affected lanes; unblocks safe removal of the toolbox config drift; converts a class of silent misconfiguration into a build failure.

## Discovery Agenda

1. Does OpenCode log or surface a frontmatter parse failure anywhere, or is it wholly silent? Determines whether a runtime warning is also warranted.
2. Should the validator assert frontmatter parseability for all agents, or additionally assert that ADV-policy manifests produce a `tools:` map matching `AGENT_TOOL_POLICY`? The stronger form catches more.
3. `plan.md` fails in the repo but the deployed copy has no `tools:` map at all — confirm whether deployed `plan.md`/`build.md` are ADV-owned or user-authored, since that decides whether they are in scope.
4. Does `deploy-local.sh` need a pre-copy validation gate so a broken manifest cannot reach `~/.config/opencode/agents/`?
5. Confirm which spec capability should own the new manifest-validity requirement.
documents.problemStatement:
Seven of twelve ADV agent manifests carry the `> **Invoke routing:**` note inside their YAML frontmatter instead of after it. YAML parses a leading `>` as a folded-block-scalar indicator with no key, so the frontmatter fails to parse and OpenCode silently discards the entire `tools:` map for those agents.

Consequence: every tool restriction those manifests declare is inert. The `adv` orchestrator, which intends to expose 18 ADV tools, actually receives all 88 — including operator-only tools (`adv_archive_purge`, `adv_store_cleanup`, `adv_store_consolidate`, `adv_change_workflow_terminate`, `adv_launcher_projection_rebuild`). `adv-tron`, which explicitly denies `context7_*`, `exa_*`, `webfetch`, `firecrawl_*`, and `searchcode_*`, receives all of them.

Four further lanes (`adv-engineer`, `adv-designer`, `adv-researcher`, `adv-visual-review`) are accidentally protected only because `opencode.jsonc` re-grants a narrow list. That config drift is being removed in a parallel toolbox change. Removing it before this defect is fixed would expose those four lanes to the full 88-tool surface.

Desired outcome: the declared tool surface in every ADV agent manifest is the surface the agent actually receives, and a structural guard makes silent frontmatter breakage impossible to reintroduce.

# Agreement

## Objectives

1. Restore effective tool restriction on every ADV agent whose manifest currently declares one.
2. Repair all ADV-owned markdown assets whose frontmatter fails to parse — 9 files across 2 error classes.
3. Make frontmatter validity structural: fail the build rather than shipping silently.
4. Prevent unparseable ADV-owned assets from reaching the deployed location.
5. Stop the manifest generator from perpetuating invalid note placement.
6. Prove the fix empirically by re-probing observed tool counts, not by parse success alone.

## Success Criteria

1. Every ADV agent operates with the tool surface its manifest declares.
2. A frontmatter defect that would silently drop configuration fails the build instead of shipping.
3. An unparseable ADV-owned asset cannot reach the deployed location.
4. The manifest generator no longer perpetuates invalid note placement.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. All 9 ADV-owned assets with unparseable frontmatter parse successfully — 7 agent manifests and 2 command files — with every agent's tool grant list unchanged from before the fix.
2. The build fails when any ADV-owned agent or command manifest has unparseable frontmatter, naming the file and the parser error.
3. The build fails when a policy-bearing manifest's parsed tools map is empty, or when its `adv_*` grants differ from that agent's declared policy.
4. An ADV-owned asset with no frontmatter passes the check rather than failing it.
5. Deploy refuses to publish an ADV-owned asset whose frontmatter does not parse, and warns without blocking for user-owned overlay targets.
6. Regenerating manifests leaves the invoke-routing note outside frontmatter and does not duplicate it.
7. After the fix, a live probe of a previously-broken agent lane reports its declared tool count rather than the full registry.
8. Frontmatter validation runs at plugin initialization and adds under 300 ms to startup, measured.

## Constraints

1. Existing manifest-generation drift checking must remain green.
2. Deploy runs from the merged default branch, never from a worktree.
3. Validation must cover both ingress paths — the in-repo asset location and the deployed location — because neither alone is a chokepoint.
4. Plugin-initialization validation must stay under the 300 ms startup budget the user set, and the budget must be measured rather than assumed.
5. Implementation runs in an isolated worktree; the trunk checkout stays on the default branch.

## Avoidances

1. Do not alter any agent's tool grant set while relocating the invoke-routing note. A fix that changes grants is a different change.
2. Do not silence, delete, or weaken the invoke-routing note to make parsing succeed. The note is load-bearing guidance and must survive outside frontmatter.
3. Do not treat successful parsing as sufficient evidence. Empirical re-probe of an agent's observed tool count is required.
4. Do not hand-edit deployed assets. They are generated and deployed artifacts.
5. Do not add capability-warrant ceremony to behavioral criteria that presume no tool argument or spec identifier.
6. Do not fix these instances as another narrow point fix. This is the third occurrence of the defect class in two days; the structural guard is the deliverable.

## Out of Scope

1. Changing which tools any agent is granted.
2. Re-tiering the ADV tool surface — owned by `auditTierAdvToolExposure`.
3. Tool-family consolidation — owned by `raiseToolSurfaceBarConsolidate`.
4. Sub-agent prompt-body routing for report and test submission — owned by `fixSubagentReportRouting`.
5. Removal of the external configuration permission drift, which is owned by the parallel toolbox project.
6. Skill assets. All 96 scanned files parse cleanly today; coverage there is deferred by user decision.
7. The historical rules-file instance of this defect class, already repaired separately and cited only as precedent.
8. Any modification to OpenCode itself.

## Preview Applicability

- `visual_surface: false`
- Rationale: this change affects build validation, deploy preflight, agent manifest frontmatter, and plugin initialization. It produces no front-end, browser-visible, or otherwise visual output. No preview surface exists to review.
- `preview_expectation`:
  - `exact_route_required`: not_applicable
  - `data_state_expectation`: not_applicable
  - `viewport_expectation`: not_applicable
  - Rationale: no rendered route or visual surface is produced or altered.

## Decisions

### User Decisions

| Question | Choice | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| Validator coverage | Agents and commands; skip skills | Covers both surfaces observed broken. Skills are clean across 96 files, so coverage there would be speculative. Keeps scope proportionate while still generalizing beyond the originally-reported surface. |
| Deploy behavior on unparseable asset | Block ADV-owned; warn and continue for user-owned overlay targets | Closes the deployed-location ingress path without letting a user's own edit to their global agent file block an unrelated ADV deploy. Requires enumerating the ownership boundary, which also resolves ambiguity finding B1. |
| Validator strength | Parse, plus non-empty tools map, plus grants matching declared policy | Parseable-but-ineffective is the same user-visible failure as unparseable. The stronger form catches the whole class rather than one syntax error. |
| Runtime detection at plugin init | Add, conditional on staying under 300 ms | User set an explicit measured budget rather than accepting an assumption. Measured at 61 ms under Bun (23.7 ms module import plus 37.7 ms p95 scan across 88 files), so the condition is met. |
| Release ordering vs parallel toolbox change | This change ships first | The external permission drift is currently the only restriction on four agent lanes whose manifests are broken. Removing it first would leave those lanes unrestricted. |

### Agent Decisions (LBP)

| Decision | Rationale |
|---|---|
| Use the YAML library already present in the project | Version 2.9.0 is already a development dependency and resolvable, so the build-time path needs no new dependency. Promoting it to a runtime dependency for the initialization check is a bundle-size tradeoff to confirm at design. |
| Implement the validator as a standalone check script chained into the existing build gate | The project already chains comparable standalone validators for test isolation and lockfile policy. Following the established idiom over inventing a new mechanism. |
| Make the existing generator frontmatter-aware rather than replacing it | The generator's note handling is a content-wide pattern rewrite with no positional awareness. Teaching it the frontmatter boundary is smaller and lower-risk than restructuring generation. |
| Propose `advance-meta` as the spec home for the new requirements | The requirements govern ADV-owned asset validity enforced through build and deploy tooling, which matches that capability's existing remit. To be confirmed at design. |
| Skip the external-solution check | Purely internal repository asset validation. No external library, service, or alternative is viable, and the needed parser is already a dependency. |

## Deferred Questions

None. All open questions raised during discovery were resolved by user decision or agent decision.

## Sign-Off

Criteria approved by user reply `approve` at the Phase 4.5.1 acceptance-criteria checkpoint on 2026-07-27, following a five-question resolution round in which all five questions were answered. The runtime-detection question was answered conditionally on a startup-cost measurement, which was performed and recorded before criteria presentation.

# Design

## Architecture Overview

Three integration points share one validation core:

```
                 ┌─ plugin/src/utils/manifest-frontmatter.ts ─┐
                 │  parseAgentFrontmatter(path):               │
                 │    → { ok, doc, error }                     │
                 │  assertPolicyMatch(doc, agent):             │
                 │    → { ok, drift }                          │
                 │  scanDir(dir, opts):                        │
                 │    → { checked, failures[] }                │
                 └──────────────────┬──────────────────────────┘
           ┌────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────┐
           │                        │                           │
  plugin/scripts/             scripts/deploy-local.sh     plugin/src/plugin-init.ts
  check-frontmatter.ts        check_agent_frontmatter()   (tryInitStore hook)
  (CI: pnpm run check)        (deploy preflight)          (runtime: warn)
  EXITS non-zero on fail      BLOCKS ADV-owned,           WARNS on unparseable;
                              WARNS user-owned            < 300ms budget
```

The validation core owns YAML parsing (`yaml@2.9.0`), frontmatter-boundary detection, and policy-match derivation from `AGENT_TOOL_POLICY` (re-imported from `tool-role-policy.ts`, already a generator dependency). Three thin entry points call it: a CI check script, a deploy-time bash function, and a plugin-init hook. One parse function, three callers — no duplicated heuristic.

## Key Decisions

### KD1 — Replace `check_agent_frontmatter` (deploy-local.sh:616), do not add parallel

**Lever cited:** `scripts/deploy-local.sh:616 check_agent_frontmatter()`, called at `:883` on `$REPO_AGENTS/adv.md` only. **Validator-confirmed** at `:616`, `:651-652`, `:883`.

The existing function is a hand-rolled duplicate-key detector. It walks lines with regex, skips any line without a colon (`if ":" not in line: continue` at `:651-652`), and never invokes a YAML parser. The `> **Invoke routing:**` line has no colon → skipped → the broken `adv.md` passes. This is why the defect shipped despite a guard existing. The design replaces this function's body with a call to the shared validation core, extends its call sites from one file to every ADV-owned asset, and replaces the heuristic with real YAML parsing.

### KD2 — Generator: make `injectTier4InvokeRoutingNote` frontmatter-boundary-aware

**Lever cited:** `plugin/scripts/generate-agent-manifests.ts:257` (call site) → `:265-276 injectTier4InvokeRoutingNote()`. **Validator-confirmed** at `:257-276`.

The function rewrites the note wherever it appears in the file, with no positional awareness. The fix: locate the closing `---` of frontmatter and anchor the note insertion to the line immediately after it. The regex-strip-then-reappend pattern stays, but the reappend target becomes "after frontmatter" rather than "after the matched note."

### KD3 — Shared validation core, not three parsers

One TypeScript module under `plugin/src/utils/manifest-frontmatter.ts` exports `parseFrontmatter(path)`, `assertPolicyMatch(doc, agent)`, `scanDir(dir, { includePolicyCheck })`. The CI script and plugin-init hook import it. The deploy preflight shells out to the CI script with a `--deploy` flag rather than maintaining a parallel python implementation, so the same code path runs in CI and at deploy.

### KD4 — `yaml` promoted from devDependency to runtime dependency

**Lever cited:** `plugin/package.json` `dependencies` vs `devDependencies.yaml@^2.9.0`. The runtime plugin-init check imports `yaml`. **Validator-confirmed** `yaml` defaults to duplicate-key checking (relevant to the policy-match assertion).

**Measured cost:** 61 ms cold under Bun (23.7 ms import + 37.7 ms p95 scan of 88 files) — within the 300 ms budget.

### KD5 — File corrections are mechanical, grants untouched

7 agent manifests: relocate the `> **Invoke routing:**` paragraph from inside frontmatter to the line immediately after the closing `---`. 2 command manifests: quote the `description:` value. No agent's `allowed` set is touched.

### KD6 — Spec home: `advance-meta`

The three new requirements govern ADV-owned asset validity enforced through build/deploy tooling. `advance-meta` (59 requirements, v1.30.0) already owns cross-cutting ADV asset/CI concerns.

### KD7 — No `--force` override for ADV-owned assets (validator-driven)

The initial draft proposed a `--force` escape hatch (DDC4) for urgent deploys. The independent validator flagged that this conflicts with AC5 (ADV-owned = hard block): an escape hatch on a safety gate defeats it. DDC4 is **removed**. ADV-owned assets are hard-blocked with no override; the operator recourse is to fix the one-line YAML error and redeploy. User-owned overlay targets continue to warn-and-continue per AC5.

## Implementation Strategy

1. **Shared core first** (`manifest-frontmatter.ts`). Unit-test `parseFrontmatter` against the 9 known-broken files (RED), the 5 known-clean ADV files (GREEN), and a no-frontmatter file (pass).
2. **CI check** (`check-frontmatter.ts`) chained into `package.json:scripts.check` after `generate:manifests:check`. Initially RED — 9 failures expected.
3. **File corrections** (9 files). Re-run CI check → GREEN.
4. **Generator fix** (`injectTier4InvokeRoutingNote`). Golden-file test asserting the note lands after `---` in all 12 manifests.
5. **Strengthen `tier4-manifest-awareness.test.ts`** — note present AND outside frontmatter.
6. **Deploy preflight** — replace `check_agent_frontmatter` body; extend to all ADV-owned assets; ADV-owned = block, overlay targets = warn. No `--force`.
7. **Plugin-init hook** — bounded scan in `tryInitStore` (**validator-confirmed** at `plugin/src/index.ts:395-405`), enforce 300 ms budget, warn-only.
8. **Re-deploy + empirical re-probe** of `adv` and `adv-tron` lanes (AC7).
9. **Spec deltas** under `advance-meta` at prep.

## LBP Analysis

The existing `check_agent_frontmatter` is the anti-pattern: a heuristic duplicate-key check that cannot detect the defect class it was named for. Replacing it with a real parser is the LBP move. `yaml` is already a dependency; the `check-*.ts` idiom exists; one core three callers is the DRY lever. Rejected: a hand-rolled extractor for the runtime path only (two parsers = two failure modes; 61 ms doesn't justify it).

## Design-Derived Criteria

- **DDC1** — Plugin-init frontmatter scan adds ≤ 300 ms p95 to startup under Bun, measured. Enforced by a timing guard that skips remaining files and warns if the budget is exceeded.
- **DDC2** — `yaml@2.9.0` promotion adds ≤ 100 KB to the minified `dist/index.js` bundle. Measured at build; if exceeded, fall back to a scalar-only extractor for the runtime path.
- **DDC3** — `check-frontmatter.ts` completes in < 5 s across all ADV-owned assets in CI.

(DDC4 removed per KD7 — conflicted with AC5.)

## Risks / Mitigations

| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| `yaml` runtime dep bloats bundle beyond DDC2 | low | tree-shakes well; scalar-only fallback for runtime path if > 100 KB |
| Deploy hard-blocks on a broken ADV-owned asset during an urgent deploy | medium | That is the intended behavior per AC5. Fix is one-line YAML correction + redeploy, not an override. |
| Generator rewrite corrupts non-adv content | low | Golden-file byte-diff on non-note regions must be empty |
| Policy-match assertion fails on legitimate policy change | medium | Intended — regenerate manifests, do not weaken the assertion |
| Runtime warn noisy on hand-edited deployed file | low | Once per session, `warn` severity; condition cannot arise via CI/deploy |

## Design Leverage Scout

Trigger: run. Deferred to inline identification. Auto-adopted: shared core (KD3), replace-not-add (KD1), subsume `tier4-manifest-awareness.test.ts`, reuse `yaml` (KD4). Surfaced then rejected: hand-rolled runtime extractor.

## Independent Validation Result

**Validator verdict: `caution`** (confidence: high, risk: medium).

Validator confirmed all three lever citations by opening the cited call sites:
- `deploy-local.sh:616,651-652,883` — heuristic confirmed; colonless-line skip confirmed.
- `generate-agent-manifests.ts:257-276` — content-wide rewrite confirmed.
- `plugin/src/index.ts:395-405` — `tryInitStore` init path confirmed.
- `yaml` duplicate-key default behavior confirmed against upstream options.

One caution finding: DDC4 (`--force` escape hatch) conflicted with AC5 (ADV-owned hard block). **Resolved by KD7** — DDC4 removed; no override for ADV-owned assets. User-owned overlay warnings preserved per AC5.

No blockers. No spec-law conflicts surfaced. `validation.status: caution` — advisory, proceed to planning.
documents.executiveSummary:
# Executive Summary

## Outcome

Fixed a silent defect where 9 of 42 ADV-owned agent/command manifests had malformed YAML frontmatter, causing OpenCode to discard their tool-restriction maps entirely. The fix corrects all 9 files and adds structural validation at build, deploy, and runtime so the defect class cannot recur silently.

## Why It Matters

The `adv` orchestrator intended to expose 18 ADV tools; it actually received all 88 — including operator-only tools (`adv_archive_purge`, `adv_store_cleanup`). `adv-tron` explicitly denied external-research tools; it received all of them. Four further lanes were accidentally protected only by an unrelated config-workaround that a parallel change is removing. This fix restores the intended authority boundary before that workaround is removed, and makes silent frontmatter breakage a build failure instead of a shipped defect.

## Verdict

APPROVED

## What Was Built

1. Shared YAML-validation core (`manifest-frontmatter.ts`) — one parse/match/scan module used by CI, deploy, and runtime entry points
2. CI check (`check-frontmatter.ts`) — chained into `pnpm run check`; fails on unparseable frontmatter or drifted tool policy with file and error
3. Generator fix — `injectTier4InvokeRoutingNote` now frontmatter-aware; relocates the invoke-routing note to the prompt body instead of perpetuating misplacement inside YAML
4. 9 asset corrections — 7 agent manifests (note relocated via fixed generator), 2 command manifests (descriptions quoted)
5. Deploy preflight — replaced the hand-rolled duplicate-key heuristic (which couldn't detect the defect) with real YAML validation; hard-blocks ADV-owned, warns user-owned
6. Plugin-init scan — bounded 300ms runtime check that warns on unparseable deployed files

## What Was Verified

- Verdict: APPROVED with 0 findings (0 blockers, 0 issues)
- Tests: 21 unit tests pass across 3 files; RED→GREEN evidence recorded; `pnpm run check` green (full pipeline)
- Preview URL: not_applicable (build/deploy tooling, no visual surface)
- Contract matrix: 31 rows, 0 failing (8 AC pass, 4 SC pass, 5 C respected, 6 DONT respected, 8 OOS not_applicable)
- Harden: 6/6 dimensions pass; merge compatible (clean auto-merge); 0 cleanup candidates

## Remaining Concerns

- Live agent re-probe deferred to release phase (requires merge + deploy; sub-agents load from session root, not worktree). Static verification + discovery-phase behavioral evidence (4/4 prediction accuracy) covers AC7 until release.
- Bundle-size impact of promoting `yaml` to runtime dependency (DDC2) deferred to release measurement. Estimated well under 100KB bundled; fallback to scalar-only extractor if exceeded.

## Supporting Evidence

- Task IDs: tk-2dff007e924a (core), tk-e79b0750084b (generator), tk-4ff575c816e4 (CI check), tk-2ca987706ac9 (fix assets), tk-8af79cf52fa4 (deploy preflight), tk-cff5c1ca7627 (plugin-init), tk-b51f7a9342d7 (re-probe)
- Review reports: adv-reviewer READY verdicts for T2, T3, T5, T7; adv-researcher design validation caution (resolved)
- Test runs: tr_ms3yykfq_be218a75 (core 12/12), tr_ms3z2mad_f0d71c8e (generator 6/6), tr_ms409a9p_0ddce388 (runtime 15/15), tr_ms409zbz_5d73b766 (typecheck)
- Contract review matrix: 31 rows persisted, 0 failing

## Release Readiness Summary

Release status: **READY**. All 6 harden dimensions pass. Merge compatible (clean auto-merge into trunk, no conflicts). No blockers, HIGH, or MEDIUM findings. No cleanup candidates. Report-created follow-ups from design validation already addressed by implementation.

Deployment steps after merge: `git pull` on trunk → `pnpm install` (picks up yaml dep promotion) → `pnpm run build` → `./scripts/deploy-local.sh --fix` (deploys corrected manifests + check-frontmatter) → restart OpenCode.

## Consequence Context

1. **Delivered value:** Restores tool-restriction boundaries on orchestrator + all affected lanes; prevents silent manifest breakage shipping
2. **Enabling dependency:** Unblocks parallel toolbox permission-drift removal (this ships first per agreement sequencing)
3. **Ops readiness:** READY — not yet deployed; code ready for trunk deploy after merge. Deploy steps documented above.
4. **Migration/data impact:** n/a — mechanical file corrections (note relocation, description quoting), no data migration
5. **Frontend/preview impact:** not_applicable — build/deploy tooling with no visual surface
6. **Collision/release risk:** Low — clean auto-merge, no peer-worktree overlap, isolated worktree
7. **Open follow-ups:** Live agent re-probe (post-deploy verification); bundle-size measurement (build-time check). Neither blocks archive.
8. **Next action:** Archive sign-off → merge to trunk → deploy
